page: Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 128.0 GB, establishing a high density of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core execution capabilities, with stress-ng single-core testing reaching 2701.38, placing it in the top quartile of evaluated systems. Conversely, total parallel compute capacity is constrained by the four-vCPU limit, leading to lower-quartile outcomes in multi-core metrics such as stress-ng multi-core (5400.07) and Geekbench multi-core (3661.0). Large-block uncached memory operations register 38.59 GB/sec for reads and 22.83 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests show moderate throughput in text processing and compression, while Redis SET throughput reaches 4.19 million operations per second and static web throughput reaches 5.19 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration of the E16-4as_v5 offers an advantageous structure for scenarios where database or application licensing is billed per processor core. By coupling 128.0 GB of memory with only 4 vCPUs, it maximizes available memory capacity per licensed unit. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage for persistent disk access. This makes the instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute, including caching tiers, memory-resident analytics, and in-memory databases.

The system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, paired with an extensive 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated 32.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It contains no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, the instance delivers strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a top-quartile stress-ng single-core result of 2701.38, while multi-core compute metrics reflect the conservative 4-thread envelope. Memory bandwidth registers at 38.59 GB/sec for uncached reads, supporting moderate transactional throughput. By constraining the core count against a large memory footprint, this instance optimizes per-core software licensing costs. It is tailored for memory-heavy workloads with limited parallel CPU requirements, including in-memory databases, memory caching tiers, and memory-resident analytics services.
